title: Transcription factor binding sites are frequently under accelerated evolution in primates
one_liner_zh: 该文用系统发育方法检测灵长类中TFBS的加速进化，虽涉及TF-DNA结合位点但无AI/物理模拟建模，且侧重进化基因组学而非互作机制。
abstract: Recent comparative genomic studies have identified many human accelerated elements (HARs) with elevated substitution rates in the human lineage. However, it remains unknown to what extent transcription factor binding sites (TFBSs) are under accelerated evolution in humans and other primates. Here, we introduce two pooling-based phylogenetic methods with dramatically enhanced sensitivity to examine accelerated evolution in TFBSs. Using these new methods, we show that more than 6,000 TFBSs annotated in the human genome have experienced accelerated evolution in Hominini, apes, and Old World monkeys. Although these TFBSs individually show relatively weak signals of accelerated evolution, they collectively are more abundant than HARs. Also, we show that accelerated evolution in Pol III binding sites may be driven by lineage-specific positive selection, whereas accelerated evolution in other TFBSs might be driven by nonadaptive evolutionary forces. Finally, the accelerated TFBSs are enriched around neurodevelopmental and pluripotency genes, suggesting that accelerated evolution in TFBSs may drive the divergence of neurodevelopmental processes between primates.
abstract_zh: 近期比较基因组学研究已识别出许多在人类谱系中具有较高替换速率的人类加速元件（human accelerated elements, HARs）。然而，转录因子结合位点（transcription factor binding sites, TFBSs）在人类及其他灵长类动物中加速进化的程度仍属未知。在此，我们引入了两种基于池化的系统发育方法，其灵敏度显著增强，用于检测TFBSs中的加速进化。利用这些新方法，我们表明人类基因组中注释的超过6,000个TFBSs在人族（Hominini）、猿类及旧世界猴中经历了加速进化。尽管这些TFBSs个体上显示出相对较弱的加速进化信号，但它们总体上比HARs更为丰富。此外，我们显示Pol III结合位点的加速进化可能由谱系特异性正选择驱动，而其他TFBSs的加速进化则可能由非适应性进化力量驱动。最后，加速进化的TFBSs富集于神经发育和多能性基因周围，提示TFBSs中的加速进化可能驱动了灵长类之间神经发育过程的差异。
